Hi Markus —

We’re kicking off the security review for the inference path that will be handling PHI in our pilot. A few focused asks from the NovaHealth audit team so we can complete the SIG/CAIQ mapping and the SOC 2 supplement:

1) A current subprocessor roster scoped to the inference runtime (libraries, vendor services, managed caches).
2) Provenance details for the KV/prefix cache used by your runtime (who provides it, where keys live, any downstream subprocessors).
3) Any existing control artifacts that specifically address cache residency, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, and key management (SOC 2 section or CAIQ references are fine).
4) A short attestation whether you persist user-derived keys or customer-specific KMS keys for cached state.

Target timeline: can you provide the inventory and a short write-up by EOD next Friday (2025-05-09)? If not, please propose a date.

Attaching the Nova SIG v2 template and a short scope doc to this thread (audit-team will re-send if needed).

Thanks — happy to set a 30min sync if that helps.

Hi all — pulling the runtime/infra pieces together. Summary below; attaching a CSV snapshot of subprocessors and a short provenance note for the KV vendor.

Subprocessor snapshot (excerpt):
- kvcloud.io (managed KV cache service) — provides in-memory prefix/KV caching deployed in GCP us-west1 regions; contracts as a subprocessor; TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest.
- fast-io (networking mesh) — connectivity and eBPF acceleration (contracted by kvcloud).
- libjson-parse (open-source) — parsing helper bundled at build time (no network calls).

KV cache provenance (short):
- Provider: kvcloud.io (kv-support@kvcloud.io).
- Deployment: Multi-tenant managed service; our runtime uses a dedicated namespace/instance per customer for isolation.
- Keys: Ephemeral session keys are derived per request; persistent encryption keys for storage are customer-tenant keys backed by Redwood-managed KMS in GCP (we use customer-scoped key wrapping when customer provides a KMS ARN).
- Downstream subprocessors: kvcloud uses a small set of managed infra partners; for cryptographic operations they call a regional KMS (Google Cloud KMS). We have contractual subprocessor visibility in place (we store kvcloud’s subprocessor roster).

Controls references we can point you to: SOC 2 CC6 (encryption), CC7 (key management), CAIQ v2: IDM-02 (identity), CRY-01 (encryption at rest). Ben will map these to your SIG rows.

Attachments: subproc_snapshot_20250504.csv, kvcloud_provenance_note.txt

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Markus / Laura — thanks, this is very helpful and much of what we need. Two quick clarifying questions so our risk team can close the item: 

1) When you say "ephemeral session keys are derived per request", are those derived from a customer-specific root key (i.e., customer-controlled KMS) or from a Redwood root key used across customers? We need to know whether the wrapped keys are tenant-specific.
2) For kvcloud’s downstream KMS calls (Google Cloud KMS), do the KMS logs include the tenant id in the call context (so we can show key-use provenance in an audit)?

If yes to both, we can mark the cache as compliant for our use-case (PHI) and finish SIG mapping. If not, we’ll need to talk about possible mitigations (customer-managed KMS or dedicated tenancy).

Can we set a 30min call tomorrow (05/07) to walk through the key residency and log evidence? I’ve copied audit-team and we can take the call with whatever artifacts you can share — screenshots of KMS log entries or a redactable example are fine.

Thanks again — Sara
Security & Compliance Lead, NovaHealth Systems
